# 3. The model

A task has a `name` right now. You want a `title` and a `done` flag. In this chapter you reshape the table by changing a struct, and you learn what a migration is.

## Where the table came from

Open `migrations/0.0.1_create_task_table.sql`:

```sql
-- Generated by prea from the models: review it before committing.

create table if not exists "task" (
	"id" uuid not null default gen_random_uuid(),
	"name" text not null,
	primary key ("id")
);

-- prea:down
drop table "task";
```

This is a **migration**: a SQL file that changes the database. In the `dev` profile, whenever a model differs from the database, Preá writes a migration with the difference and applies it. The **model** is `preas/task/model.go`, and this file is its translation to SQL.

Two settings in `config/application-dev.yaml` turn this on:

```yaml
database:
  migrations:
    from_models: true # a model change becomes a migration at startup...
    on_start: true # ...that is applied right away
```

`prea new --with-db` writes them for you. The base `application.yaml` leaves both off, so only `dev` writes and applies migrations. You'll see why in [chapter 7](./configuration).

::: warning No migration in `migrations/`?
If you created the project without `--with-db` and added the database by hand, these two lines are missing, and Preá writes nothing. Add them to `config/application-dev.yaml` and restart `prea dev`. To write a migration yourself, see [Migrations](../guide/migrations#write-one-yourself).
:::

## Start the table over

This migration only exists on your machine, so you can still throw it away. Stop `prea dev` with Ctrl+C, then undo it and delete it:

```bash
prea migrate down
rm migrations/0.0.1_create_task_table.sql
```

```
undid 0.0.1_create_task_table (5ms)
```

`prea migrate down` ran the part below `-- prea:down`, and the table is gone.

::: warning Only on your machine
Once a migration is committed and others have applied it, never edit or delete it. Write a new one instead.
:::

## Change the model

Replace `preas/task/model.go`:

```go
package task

// Task is one thing to do.
type Task struct {
	ID    string `json:"id" pk:"" generated:"uuid"`
	Title string `json:"title" size:"200"`
	Done  bool   `json:"done" default:"false"`
}

func (Task) Table() string {
	return "task"
}
```

Each tag describes the column:

- `pk:""` makes `id` the primary key, and `generated:"uuid"` lets the database generate it.
- `size:"200"` limits the title to 200 characters.
- `default:"false"` makes new tasks start as not done.
- `title` is `not null` because a `string` can't be nil. A `*string` would allow null.

## Change the request bodies

The files in `dtos/` describe what clients send. Replace `preas/task/dtos/create_request.go`:

```go
package dtos

// CreateRequest is the body of POST /task.
type CreateRequest struct {
	Title string `json:"title" binding:"required"`
}
```

And `preas/task/dtos/update_request.go`:

<<< @/examples/todo/preas/task/dtos/update_request.go#update

The fields of the update are pointers on purpose. You'll see why in the next chapter.

## Fix the service

The service still talks about `Name`. In `preas/task/service.go`, change the `Create` method:

```go
func (s *Service) Create(ctx context.Context, req dtos.CreateRequest) (Task, error) {
	req.Name = strings.TrimSpace(req.Name) // [!code --]
	if req.Name == "" { // [!code --]
		return Task{}, core.NewError(http.StatusBadRequest, "name can't be blank") // [!code --]
	req.Title = strings.TrimSpace(req.Title) // [!code ++]
	if req.Title == "" { // [!code ++]
		return Task{}, core.NewError(http.StatusBadRequest, "title can't be blank") // [!code ++]
	}
	return s.Repo.Create(ctx, req)
}
```

And make `Update` hand the request straight to the repository:

```go
func (s *Service) Update(ctx context.Context, id string, req dtos.UpdateRequest) (Task, error) {
	req.Name = strings.TrimSpace(req.Name) // [!code --]
	return s.Repo.Update(ctx, id, req)
}
```

## Run it

```bash
prea dev
```

```
level=SUCCESS msg="database: generated a migration from the models: review it before committing" file=migrations/0.0.1_create_task_table.sql
level=INFO msg="database: applied 0.0.1_create_task_table (5ms)"
```

A fresh `0.0.1_create_task_table.sql`, now with your columns:

```sql
create table if not exists "task" (
	"id" uuid not null default gen_random_uuid(),
	"title" varchar(200) not null,
	"done" bool not null default false,
	primary key ("id")
);
```

```bash
curl -X POST localhost:8000/task -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title": "Buy coffee"}'
```

```json
{
    "code": 1,
    "data": {
        "id": "4caff630-444a-4a86-bb31-3b5e963cfb32",
        "title": "Buy coffee",
        "done": false
    }
}
```

`done` came from the database default.

## What you learned

- The model describes the table, and its tags describe the columns.
- In `dev`, Preá turns model changes into migrations and applies them.
- Review every migration; a local one can still be undone and regenerated.
